id: title:Gilbert09:keep a mid stream vitess grpc cancellation retryable

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion worker reliability: P1.F1.H1 classifies transient gRPC connection closures as retryable errors, while P1.F2.H1 adds a regression test. This could reduce unnecessary failure tracking and transient ingestion failures, though actual benefit depends on unverified production behavior.
review.reason: P1.F1.H1 adds a gRPC error classification and rationale; P1.F2.H1 adds a corresponding test. This is a bounded, substantive improvement with relevant checks, but no production or adoption evidence.
review.uncertainty: This chunk lacks production or adoption evidence; tier 2 is assigned based on implementation and checks, not observed benefit.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 adds a retryable error classification and its rationale. P1.F2.H1 adds a corresponding test. The chunk is complete enough to assess. No abstention needed.

observations.behavior: Adds a new entry to the set of retryable errors, including a specific gRPC error message and its rationale.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the MySQL warehouse ingestion worker to recognize a transient, self-healing gRPC connection closure during a streaming query and treat it as a retryable error rather than a terminal failure, preventing unnecessary error-tracking noise.

observations.behavior: Adds a unit test asserting that the newly classified gRPC error is recognized as retryable.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection for the retryable error classification, ensuring the worker does not treat transient connection closures during warehouse ingestion as permanent failures.
